How to do itLeg Extension

Knee lockout

Right
NOT LOCKED
Wrong
LOCKED

Right: Legs straight, knees not locked.

Wrong: Knees locked or hyperextended at the top.

Knees line up with the machine's pivot.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Back archesThe lower back arches as the legs extend.
  2. Back off padThe back lifts off the back pad.
Extend2 s
Hold1 s
Lower2 s
Look closer

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the front of your thighs.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansArching your lower back can lead to discomfort.

    FixBrace your abs. Keep your back pressed into the pad.

  • Usually meansFeeling it here, not in the quads, can mean a form error.

    FixStop if you feel pain or discomfort. Reassess your form.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Knees at the pivot. Pad on your lower shins, just above ankles.

  2. 2

    Sit back against the pad, knees bent about 90 degrees.

  3. 3

    Hold the handles at your sides. Brace your abs.

  4. 4

    Breathe out and lift with your quads, don't kick. Pause briefly.

  5. 5

    Breathe in and lower slowly with control.

Risks and when to stop

  • Locking your knees at the top can add stress to the knee.
  • Arching your lower back can lead to discomfort.
  • Too much weight can increase injury risk and likely leads to excess momentum.

Knee pain

Severe pain, badly swollen, changed shape, locking, giving way, or can't put weight on it? Get it checked today.

No better after a few weeks? See a doctor.

Back pain

Pain, numbness, tingling or weakness in both legs? Numb genitals or anus? Bladder, bowel or sexual changes? Chest pain? Serious accident? Get emergency help now. Sudden severe or fast-worsening pain? Hot, cold, shivery or unwell? See a doctor today.

No better in a few weeks? See a doctor.

General guidance, not medical advice. If something hurts, stop and get it checked.

How to do itLying Leg Curl

Hips on pad

Right
HIPS ON PAD
Wrong
HIPS LIFTING

Right: Front of the hips pressed into the pad.

Wrong: Hips lifting off the pad.

Line your knees up with the machine's axis.

Tells
  1. Low back archesYour lower back arches as your legs curl.
Curl1 s
Hold1 s
Lower3 s
Look closer

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the back of your thighs.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansArching the lower back can cause back pain and discomfort.

    FixBrace your abs. Use a lighter weight if your low back moves.

  • FixStop if the pain is sharp. Try a lighter load or a different pad position.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Lie face down, knees near the bench edge, aligned with the axis.

  2. 2

    Roller on your lower calf, not pressing your heel or Achilles.

  3. 3

    Hold the handles, abs tight. Breathe out to curl, in to lower.

  4. 4

    Start knees nearly straight, not forced locked. Curl toward your glutes.

  5. 5

    Stop before your hips lift. Lower with control, stack never touching.

Risks and when to stop

  • Line your knees up with the machine's axis to prevent joint stress.
  • Arching your lower back can cause back pain and discomfort.
  • Sudden, jerking movements can lead to injury.

Knee pain

Severe pain, badly swollen, changed shape, locking, giving way, or can't put weight on it? Get it checked today.

How to do itStanding Leg Curl

Knee steady

Right
KNEE IN PLACE
Wrong
KNEE MOVES

Right: Knee stays in place as the leg curls.

Wrong: Knee travelling forward and back each rep.

Full curl

Right
FOOT ABOVE KNEE
Wrong
CUT SHORT

Right: Foot higher than the knee at the top.

Wrong: Range cut short.

Keep your knee steady as it bends and straightens.

Curl1 s

Look closer

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the back of your thigh, strongest at the top.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansArching the lower back can cause back pain and discomfort.

    FixAvoid arching: contract your abs.

  • FixStop the set if you feel pain here.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Set the pad just above the heel of your working leg.

  2. 2

    Thighs against the support pad. Hold the handles for balance.

  3. 3

    Plant your other foot firmly. Keep your upper body still.

  4. 4

    Curl until your foot is higher than your knee. Hold a second.

  5. 5

    Don't drop it: lower slowly, straighten fully. Finish one leg, then switch.

Risks and when to stop

  • Arching your lower back can cause back pain and discomfort.
  • Sudden, jerking movements can lead to injury.
  • Too much weight makes you use momentum and body swinging.

How to do itCable Kickback

Braced back

Right
BACK FLAT
Wrong
BACK ARCHES

Right: Hinged forward, back flat, core braced.

Wrong: Lower back arching as the leg kicks back.

Brace so your lower back does not arch as the leg goes back.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Lower back archesYour lower back arches as the leg kicks back.
Kick back1 s
Hold1 s
Return2 s
Look closer

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the glute of your working leg.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansPoor form can bring in the lower back.

    FixPull your belly button in and flatten your back.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Set the pulley lowest. Strap the cuff around your working ankle.

  2. 2

    Face and hold the machine. Hinge forward, weight on the other leg.

  3. 3

    Brace your trunk. Use your hands and free leg to stay still.

  4. 4

    Leg long, knee slightly bent. Hips level, toe pointing straight down.

  5. 5

    Drive back as far as you can. Squeeze, pause, return slowly.

Risks and when to stop

  • Heavy loading breaks your form down quickly on this long lever.
  • Can't lift without swinging the leg? Use a lighter weight.
  • Twisting your hips lifts the leg higher but makes it less effective.

How to do itResisted Hip Flexion

Upright torso

Right
STAND TALL
Wrong
LEANS BACK

Right: Torso upright, thigh at hip height.

Wrong: Torso leaning back, lower back arched.

Stand tall with the core braced and the standing leg steady.

  1. Leans backYou lean back to lift the leg higher.

Lift2 s
Hold2 s
Lower2 s
Look closer

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the front of your hip and your lower belly.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansLeaning back or arching to lift higher.

    FixStand tall, core tight.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Strap the cuff to one ankle on a low cable.

  2. 2

    Face away from the machine, a little tension. Hold the frame.

  3. 3

    Brace your trunk, stand tall, hips level and square.

  4. 4

    Drive the knee straight up and forward, thigh about level. Don't swing.

  5. 5

    Pause, lower with control, no stack slam. Switch legs after the set.

Risks and when to stop

  • Don't arch your lower back to lift higher. Keep a neutral spine.
  • Acute hip or lower-back pain? Skip this exercise.
  • Stop if balance causes strain.
